annotation.title_clean: The Principal Japanese AI and Robot Law. Strategy and Research toward Establishing Basic Principles
annotation.title_en: The Principal Japanese AI and Robot Law. Strategy and Research toward Establishing Basic Principles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Association of Law and Information Systems (J-STAGE article)
annotation.venue: Journal of the Association of Law and Information Systems (ALIS), vol. 3
annotation.summary_en: Abstract of a 2018 Japanese journal article surveying Japanese AI and robot law, strategy and research trends toward establishing basic legal principles. It warns that autonomous AI-controlled robots and automated vehicles require legal re-examination, especially information security, as AI risks extend to physical danger.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI and robots are currently tools operating per human intentions.
Widespread autonomous robots require thorough legal re-examination.
Information security countermeasures for intelligent robots must be scrutinized.
Internet-era security problems could recur with AI, with added physical danger.
Surveys Japanese AI and robot law, strategy and research toward basic principles.
